title: Gael · the war and the keeping
dek: Expedition, costly living ground and the work inherited after victory.

facts.Dates: Source chronology; uncertain intervals remain explicit

body:
Gael’s campaign joins two obligations: opening a road through devastation and keeping life possible afterward. Neither its battle history nor its restoration can be reduced to one figure’s achievement.

The expedition and the limits of refuge

Gartina’s June account credits Nienna with the ship and crew that started the expeditionary chain. It is a personal explanation of why she joined and a meaningful record of initiative. It is not proof that the expedition, its discoveries or Gael’s later restoration belonged to Nienna alone.

The Tower, its sanctuary and Huoth’s guidance make repeated expeditions possible without making the island safe. Quake states a duty to protect the land and its people. That obligation is broader than defeating an enemy, and its costs appear before a stable settlement exists.

The 9 July Plains of Trial scene directly records Nienna’s death against soul eaters and wraiths and Saray recovering her body. The following quest testimony still treats Nienna as dead and the diamond offering as a plan. On 15 July, Saray obtains the diamond at Nuru’s altar and Elenia casts Raise Dead; Nienna wakes. Their actions complete the earlier recovery effort before the separate September sacrifice.

A living foothold has a collective cost

At Hope in August, Gartina weeps at the living ground while Dale immediately asks how it can be protected. Their responses show why restoration and defense cannot be separated: the green place is both an achievement and a new responsibility.

During the September Hallowing, Nienna turns toward the horde while the casters still need time. The later narration records the spell completing and life expanding. Adelia, Gartina and Elenia bear exhaustion from sustaining the work. Nienna’s final defense remains consequential beside the casters, guards and companions rather than becoming a substitute for their actions.

The outcome can be narrated without inventing a universal rule of sacrifice. Participants act toward a hoped-for result before they can know its completion. The later landscape does not retroactively give them certainty or establish that one person alone created Hope.

Victory does not recover everyone

Akarian’s relic trial places preparation inside grief. He describes work undertaken with Huoth, tests the company and directs the rings to Elenia after choices that include Dale and Saray’s devotion. The trial concerns responsibility as well as strength; it supplies no permanent ownership rule for every relic.

The November assault is devastating. Wrath cleaves Elenia; Wren offers herself to spare the others and Vaemyr hears another threatened separation. Saray’s last shot is followed by the narrator’s description of Wrath collapsing and Scribonia’s observation of her final blow. Those receipts preserve her decisive part while retaining the losses and the company around her.

Gartina immediately runs to gather Elenia’s remains. The scene gives recovery work a place beside victory. In the subsequent Sanctum scene on 21 November, Gartina casts Reincarnate and Elenia returns still a satyr. This answers the earlier return gap without making every later danger in Gael disappear.

The landscape still needs people

December restoration makes the relationship between magic and material work unusually clear. Gartina plants her staff and narration describes the pine that becomes Stake. A further seed action produces the forest; her later thanks to Krone retain the limestone transport that helped make the work possible. Her immediate concern about whether the forest will hold must remain beside the eventual landscape.

When Jiangshi calls Adelia the true Hope in her eyes, Adelia answers that hope belongs to everyone. These are compatible personal interpretations, not evidence that later transformation grants Adelia exclusive authorship of the earlier restoration.

By February 2025, Gartina chooses to remain for refugees and the new forest even while wanting to rejoin her companions. Later damage to Hope and renewed sanctuary work extend this obligation into another generation. Victory opens the possibility of keeping Gael; it does not complete it. Fenwick’s later guide remains traveler testimony, including incompatible width and radius estimates that cannot fix the atlas.
